item.title: Big Read: East Africa spent 2026 adding charges to the room. A platform has started taking a cut of them.
item.description: Booking.com has moved government taxes into the base on which it calculates commission. The Caribbean has spent six months fighting it and won carve-outs for others. East Africa, which has layered more levies onto the room this year than any region on the continent, has not asked a single question.

item.title: Big Read: The world's largest seller of hotel rooms guided its next quarter down to 1 per cent. It did not blame the room.
item.description: Booking Holdings reported 7 per cent room-night growth on 3 November and told the market to expect 1 to 3 per cent in the fourth quarter, naming elevated airfares and reduced route capacity on long-haul routes as the cause. East Africa sells almost nothing but long-haul. The same month's aviation data shows African carriers adding international capacity faster than they fill it, at the lowest load

item.title: Big Read: Europe put a clock on the money your lodge pays back. Nobody set one on the money it is owed.
item.description: A statutory instrument laid in Westminster and a directive signed in Brussels have both written a refund deadline into the supplier's side of the package holiday contract, 14 days in Britain from April 2027 and seven days under EU law. Neither says a word about when the supplier gets paid in the first place. East Africa is signing the contracts that cross those dates right now.

item.title: Big Read: East Africa sells 2027 in three days at ExCeL. The hard part is getting into the room.
item.description: World Travel Market opens in London on Tuesday with Africa back on the main exhibition floor and eight East African businesses sharing one association stand. A year ago, 12 of the 14 Ugandan operators who had paid for space were refused UK visas, and no regional board has yet published what it spends to be in that building or what it brings home.

item.title: Big Read: Hilton reported its Africa region down 5.6 per cent. It was not measuring Africa.
item.description: Three of the four listed hotel majors reported the same overlapping geography this month. Hilton's Middle East and Africa line fell 5.6 per cent and is guided to a low double-digit decline for the year, IHG's wider EMEAA bucket rose 5.0 per cent, and Accor published its numbers twice, once with the Middle East in and once with it out. item.title: Big Read: East Africa is counting cruise ships. The number that pays is bed nights.
item.description: Mombasa's record 2025/26 cruise season delivered 4,889 passengers across nine calls, under four per cent of a single month's air arrivals into Zanzibar, and almost none of them slept ashore. The published schedule for the season now opening shows four calls and not one turnaround. The region is lobbying for berths when the thing that converts a day call into a bed night is scheduled lift.

item.title: Big Read: Africa is now 47 per cent of Kenya's arrivals. The rate card is still written for Europe.
item.description: Seventy Ugandan hoteliers spent six days on the Kenyan coast this week and three trade associations signed memoranda in Mombasa, but the region's largest source market is the one East Africa's commercial architecture, priced in dollars and sold through overseas intermediaries, is least equipped to serve.

item.title: Big Read: Nobody will ask your lodge to change its name. That is what the brands are now selling East Africa.
item.description: On one Tuesday last week the world's hotel groups told investors that their growth now comes from buildings they do not own and names they do not change. East Africa's independents are the buildings, and the fine print is about distribution, not identity.

item.title: Big Read: East Africa's lodges hedged the room rate. The plate is the open position.
item.description: Kenya's maize harvest has fallen to a seven-year low, food inflation is running at 9.5 per cent, and the strongest El Nino since 1950 is landing on the region's granary. Full-board rates for 2027 are already contracted. The cost inside them is not.

item.title: Big Read: Zanzibar got the seats it asked for. The room rate fell 18 per cent.
item.description: Airline capacity into Zanzibar rose 11 per cent in a year and is forecast to rise another 33 per cent by March. August set an arrivals record at an estimated 92.9 per cent bed occupancy. Over the same twelve months the weighted average online room rate fell about 18 per cent, in every category.
